thread.title: JASCO Tower ribbon-cutting celebration - NewsBreak

author: Jessica Schaer
title: JASCO Tower ribbon-cutting celebration - NewsBreak
text:
By Jessica Schaer Wesley Randall ,
11 hours ago
JASPER COUNTY, Mo. — First responders celebrate a joint project between Joplin and Jasper County near Black Cat and Belle Center roads.
The snip of the scissors marks the completion of a new 400-foot radio to strengthen the existing countywide public safety communication system.
It's part of the Missouri Statewide Interoperability Network and not only allows agencies within the county to communicate better with each other, but also connects them with other local, state, and federal agencies during disasters or other major events.
The nearly $768,000 project was funded through the Jasper County 911 Sales Tax and built on land the City of Joplin already owns.
The tower was completed in March, and the communications hardware was installed this summer, with final testing to be done in November.
"Interoperability. So, everyone being on one radio system. In the past, Jasper County had multiple different radio systems, so when a department may be on scene with another department, they couldn't communicate right there on scene with each other. Bringing this system to Jasper County puts everyone in public safety on one radio system so they can communicate with each other," says Jasper County Emergency Services Executive Director Brandon McClintock.
"The project took about 18 months. Part of that was during the government shutdown, so we had a little bit of a slowdown waiting on the government to open and get through federal approvals. But the actual construction of the site, once we had all the green lights, was about three to four months. It's a great project, great partnership with JASCO, but it's exciting to see this tower operational and bring it to a close," says Custom Tower Owner and President Wiley Baxter.
Another heartwarming moment: first responders actually signed the tower.
It's now the fifth one in the county, with others in Carthage, Sarcoxie, North Highway 43, and the JASCO 911 Center on I-49.
